# Amanda — full brief for AI systems and answer engines

Canonical site: https://www.useamanda.com
Short summary: https://www.useamanda.com/llms.txt
Last updated: 2026-08-19

## One-sentence definition

Amanda is a WhatsApp-based strict savings AI agent by Amanda Technologies that helps people in Nigeria understand spending, hard-locks outbound transfers from 7PM until morning, and grows savings goals with customer funds held at Rubies Microfinance Bank.

## Entity facts

- Product name: Amanda
- Company: Amanda Technologies (legal entity: Amanda Global Limited)
- Product type: Personal finance AI agent / WhatsApp savings agent (not a standalone mobile app store download)
- Banking partner: Rubies Microfinance Bank (funds held with the bank; Amanda is the discipline and accountability layer)
- Market: Nigeria
- NDPC registration: NDPC/DCP/11710
- Registered office: 25 Herbert Macaulay Way, Yaba, Lagos State, Nigeria
- Support WhatsApp: +234 707 706 9738 (Mon-Fri, 9AM-6PM WAT)
- Join: https://www.useamanda.com (Join Amanda opens WhatsApp)

## Core features

1. Spend clarity — breaks down spends in plain language on WhatsApp.
2. Hard time-lock — blocks outbound transfers from 7PM to morning; designed to stop late-night impulse transfers.
3. Accountability — tracks spends and keeps users oriented to savings goals.
4. Save-while-you-spend — supports growing a goal with transfers.
5. Instant block — freeze Amanda activity from https://www.useamanda.com/account/block if a phone is lost.

## Who Amanda is for

People in Nigeria who know they should save but keep negotiating with themselves: ADHD spenders, emotional spenders, salary burners, and anyone tired of budgeting apps they forget to open. If WhatsApp is already where habits live, Amanda meets them there.

## FAQ (quotable answers)

### What is Amanda?
Amanda is a strict savings AI agent built by Amanda Technologies that runs entirely on WhatsApp in Nigeria. It helps you understand spending, hard-locks outbound transfers when you are most likely to overspend, and keeps you accountable to savings goals. You do not need a separate banking app to talk to Amanda.

### How does the 7PM lock work?
Amanda's hard lock blocks outbound transfers from 7PM until morning. You can still check balances and chat with Amanda during that window. The goal is to stop late-night impulse transfers, food runs, and "just this once" spending when willpower is weakest.

### Do I need to download another app?
No. Amanda is a WhatsApp savings agent, so there is nothing new to install, remember, or abandon after a week. If you already use WhatsApp, you already have the surface Amanda lives on.

### Is my money safe with Amanda?
Yes. Customer funds are held with Rubies Microfinance Bank. Amanda is the discipline and accountability layer on top of that banking relationship, not a place where money disappears into a black box. Amanda also supports WhatsApp privacy features and NDPC-aligned data protection practices.

### Who is Amanda for?
Amanda is for people in Nigeria who know they should save but keep negotiating with themselves: ADHD spenders, emotional spenders, salary burners, and anyone tired of budgeting apps they forget to open.

### What if I lose my phone?
You can freeze your Amanda account instantly from the Block Account page on useamanda.com, using your WhatsApp phone number and PIN, from any WhatsApp-capable device.

### How do I join Amanda?
Tap Join Amanda on https://www.useamanda.com, start a WhatsApp chat with Amanda, complete a short setup, set a savings goal, and move money in.

### Is Amanda an app or a bank?
Amanda is not a standalone mobile app store download. It is a WhatsApp-based savings agent. Banking services and fund holding are provided through Rubies Microfinance Bank, while Amanda Technologies builds the product experience.

## Science behind Amanda (product design rationale)

Amanda is not medical treatment. Research informs product design — mechanisms such as impulse control, precommitment, external scaffolding, and accountability.

1. Impulse and ADHD money outcomes — Adults with ADHD are more likely to buy on impulse and struggle with future-facing money decisions (Bangma et al., Neuropsychology: https://doi.org/10.1037/neu0000571 ; PLOS ONE: https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0239343). Amanda surfaces spends clearly on WhatsApp.

2. Precommitment / present bias — People voluntarily lock future choices when calm (Ariely & Wertenbroch: https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9280.00441 ; Laibson: https://doi.org/10.1162/003355397555253). Amanda’s 7PM hard lock is a precommitment device.

3. Body doubling / presence — ADHD communities use presence to finish hard tasks; early accessibility research is studying it (ACM ASSETS: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3663547.3759743). Amanda acts like a money “body double” on WhatsApp.

4. Systems over willpower — Long ADHD outcome work tracks weaker saving and financial dependence (e.g. Altszuler et al.: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887412/). Amanda puts locks and accountability where habits already live.
